pcs.pc_description: Obtain the shift and work schedule from the supervisor with the total number of packaging to be completed for the day.
Calculate the raw materials required for each type of product packaging.
Collect a list from the supervisor with details of the type of packaging material, the size of the packaging case to be used, and the desired weight range of each product.
Recognise variations among packages of different products.
Remove any unnecessary items from the area to make space for the items to be packaged.
Perform a quick safety inspection of the workplace.
Clean up any spills or breakages.

modules.module_title: Assess requirements and collect necessary items

pcs.pc_description: Assess the Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) required based on the product and the work environment.
Collect and wear all the necessary PPE.
Check the availability of additional tools, such as tape guns and their condition.
Visually check the condition of packaging equipment.
Examine whether the machine operating settings are correct. If any changes are found, adjust the settings according to the schedule.
Check for the calibration and validation tags on the packaging equipment.
Ensure that there are sufficient raw materials such as tapes and sealants.
Load the raw materials into the packaging machine.
Ensure sensors and guides are clean and functioning to prevent misfeeds.
Read the user Manual and follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the safety and functionality of the specific model.
Confirm the machine is connected to the appropriate power source and the electrical components are intact.
Switch on packaging equipment and wait till it is warmed up.
Perform a test run or trial packing and Recalibrate the machine settings if required.
Report to the supervisor if a problem cannot be fixed.

pcs.pc_description: Set the machine’s feeding speed according to the product's type, size, weight and handling requirements.
Check that the goods to be packed are in their appropriate packaging cases.
Visually inspect the goods to be packed for damage or defects.
Ensure the packaging cases are ready, lined up within reach, adequately stacked, and free from obstructions.
Make any necessary adjustments for spacing between items to avoid jams.
Follow the manufacturer’s guidelines for loading.
Place the products onto the feed conveyor or designated area of the packaging machine.
Use the packaging equipment to seal the packaging cases in an optimal manner.
Weigh the package to determine if it is within the allowed limits.
Report errors and discrepancies, if any, to the supervisor.
Remove the sealed package from the packaging machine.
Follow guidelines concerning handling and moving sealed packages to the labelling area or hand them over to carpenters if required.
Perform labelling or handover the sealed packages to a labeller for labelling as per company policy.
Collect sealed packages from the labelling area and cross-check the product in the packing case.
Paste all the required labels straight onto the packing case in the right areas and Ensure they’re fully adhered.
Avoid overlapping with other labels or packaging details.
Review each labelled product to ensure all information is correct and matches the reference.
Move labelled packages to the finished packages area.
Keep any unused labels in a designated area to prevent damage or loss.
Dispose of any label scraps or mistakes appropriately to maintain a tidy workspace.
Continuously check for jams or misfeeds.
Perform corrective measures, such as pressing the reset button, if a machine jams or the conveyor gets stuck.
Reload the sealant if the machine stops due to insufficient sealant.
Identify packages left unpacked and place them near the end of the line to be sealed again.
Ensure the machine is not operated beyond rated capacity in case of a breakdown.
Report to the supervisor in case of discrepancies like accidents.

Clean and inspect the packaging equipment to ensure it is fit for the next day's operations.
Perform routine maintenance, such as lubricating moving parts, checking belts, and inspecting sensors.
Dispose of waste materials, such as damaged labels, packing cases, etc., safely as per the waste management policy of the company.

Clean up any spills or breakages.
Return any PPE, tools, materials and equipment used to their storage racks.

Restock packaging supplies as needed to ensure readiness for the next shift.
Complete any forms as management requires, such as packaging machine status, shift status, etc.
Maintain Batch Packaging Record (BPR), including packaging process-related logbooks and documents.

pcs.pc_description: Collect maintenance schedule from the supervisor and arrange for necessary tools, such as wrenches, screwdrivers, cleaning supplies, and lubricants.
In case of a machine overhaul, plan maintenance in advance and recommend it during holidays or non-peak hours.
Check the manufacturer’s instruction manual for specific maintenance instructions and safety precautions.
Examine for any visible signs of wear or damage, such as frayed belts, leaks, or loose components.
Observe the overall functioning of the packaging machine to identify any problems with material flow, quality of output, cycle time analysis, power and controls, etc.
Make any minor adjustments in settings or parameters if required to ensure smooth functioning.
Clean packaging equipment and remove debris, dust, or product residues from the machine’s surfaces, including belts, hoppers, and control panels.
Apply appropriate lubricants to bearings, gears, and other moving parts as specified in the manual.
Inspect the Electrical Components, such as wiring and connections, for any signs of wear or damage.
Ensure that all safety features like safety alarms and indicators, etc., are functioning properly.
Verify that the machine is correctly calibrated for product measurements, speeds, and settings.
Replace any parts that have worn out at the times specified by the manufacturer.
Assess the packaging machine and escalate to the supervisor if there is a likelihood of future problems; replacement of parts or service from a specialised technician is required.
Complete and check off all the line items in the preventive maintenance checklist.
Test run the packaging equipment to ensure that it is fully functional and safe for use.
Record all maintenance performed, including dates, completed tasks, and replaced parts.
Clean the area after maintenance activity.

modules.module_title: Print Labels using a label maker or printer

pcs.pc_description: Check the settings of label maker/ printer.
Load necessary label roll/ tape/ label sheets, etc.
Check alignment and format by printing sample labels.
Print the required labels according to the labelling schedule.
Cut the labels according to the required size and shape in case the labels are printed in a roll.

modules.module_title: Prepare and set up Labelling Machine

pcs.pc_description: Follow the steps involved in the Prepare for Packaging process.
Check for any visible signs of wear or damage on the machine and make sure that all parts, such as the rollers, sensors, and label applicators, are in good condition.
Ensure there is no debris or leftover material from previous runs, which could cause issues during labelling.
Place the roll of labels onto the machine, ensuring it is loaded correctly with the right orientation.
Ensure the labels are properly wound on the spool and the leading edge is aligned with the feeding mechanism.
Adjust the label roll tension to avoid over or underfeeding of labels.
Confirm the labels are the correct size for the product being labelled. The machine may have adjustable label length, width, and position settings.
Make sure that the product is placed correctly on the conveyor or labelling station and aligned properly for certain machines to avoid label misapplication.
Adjust the position of the label on the product (e.g., front, back, or wraparound labelling).
Input the correct label size (height and width) into the machine's control panel so it applies the label correctly.
Set the desired labelling speed, which should match the product flow on the conveyor.
Adjust the sensor to recognise the exact position of the product to trigger the labelling mechanism.
Set the applicator head (roller, tamp, or blow) to the correct position of the labelling product.
Confirm that the applicator will cover the entire product circumference if it's a wraparound labelling machine.
Start the Machine and Monitor the Labeling Process.
Ensure that labels are placed at the right spot on the product or package, and Adjust the Speed if Needed.
Regularly inspect the position of labels on the products to ensure they are applied correctly (e.g., not skewed, at the right location).
Ensure that labels are not wrinkled or bubbling up, which can affect the product’s appearance and presentation.
Verify that the label is securely adhered to and that the adhesive is applied effectively.
Perform the steps involved in Post Packaging Activities.

modules.module_title: Prepare and Set up the Case Packer/Palletizer

pcs.pc_description: Follow the steps involved in the Prepare for Packaging process.
Ensure that the correct size cases are used or set the machine to adjust to different sizes automatically.

modules.module_title: Load Products into the Case Packer

pcs.pc_description: Ensure products are aligned according to the packing requirements (e.g., standing or lying down).
Place empty cases (boxes) in the machine’s loading area.
Turn on the case packer and ensure that the product feeder and robotic arms (if applicable) work properly.
Adjust the machine’s speed to ensure smooth operation.
Watch for jams, misalignments, or malfunctioning components.
Occasionally check the packed cases to ensure they meet quality standards.
Unload the Packed Cases from the case packer and transfer them to the palletizer.
Ensure that the palletizer arranges and stacks the packed cases onto a pallet according to the specified stacking pattern.
Confirm that the palletizer stacks the boxes in multiple layers according to the size of the cases and weight, ensuring stability and weight distribution.
If the case packer or palletizer jams, stop the machine, remove the obstruction, and restart once the issue is resolved.
Handle Error Codes or error messages displayed on the control panel and follow the troubleshooting guide to resolve issues.
Be familiar with the emergency stop button and how to use it.
Ensure the equipment is locked out and tagged out when performing maintenance or repairs.
Perform the steps involved in Post Packaging Activities.

modules.module_title: Prepare and Set up the Stretch Wrapping/ Strapping Machine

pcs.pc_description: Follow the steps involved in the Prepare for Packaging process.
Set Parameters and modify the settings based on the type of product being wrapped or strapped.
Adjust the number of film layers, stretch percentage, and wrapping speed.
Align the tension, strap width, and the number of straps to be applied for the strapping machine.
Ensure that the product or pallet is properly placed in the machine’s loading area and that the load is stable and centered.
Position the pallet or product correctly on the turntable or conveyor belt (depending on the machine type).
Turn on the machine by pressing the start button or following the instructions for the machine.
Ensure the pallet rotates and the film is applied to the product as it spins on the turntable.
Check that the film is threaded correctly through the machine and that the machine automatically applies the wrap.
Adjust film tension or wrapping speed Manually based on the product size and requirements.
Confirm that there’s a consistent overlap with each film layer and that the load is secure.
Ensure 2-3 full film turns are done for proper security or add as required.
Place the strapping coil onto the machine.
Verify that the strap is aligned properly so it feeds through the machine without jamming.
Set down the pallet or load in the designated area for strapping.
Press the start button or foot pedal to activate the strapping machine once the product is stable and aligned.
Ensure the machine applies the strap around the load, automatically tensioning, sealing, and cutting it.
Adjust the strap tension (some machines allow for manual or automatic tensioning) to ensure the strap is tight enough to secure the load without damaging the product.
Ensure the wrapping or strapping is consistent throughout the process, with no gaps or loose areas.
If the film isn't applying evenly, check the film’s tension or alignment and ensure there are no obstructions in the machine's path.
Watch the strap’s tension to avoid over- tightening or under-tightening, as either can be problematic.
